reviewer: AI reviewer (Claude), not a person; a person should spot-check these verdicts
method: 20 random REQUIRES/TEACHES edges from the graph after the concept review (throughline.quality.sample_edges, seed 2026). Each judged strictly against the talk's title, stated level and abstract: is the concept really required (or taught) as claimed, and is it central rather than a side mention? 'partly' counts as not correct.
judged_on: 2026-10-24, graph with 55 concepts and 400 REQUIRES/TEACHES edges

edges.evidence: connects Figma and GitHub Copilot through MCP
edges.reason: The talk demos a Figma-to-Copilot planning workflow that runs over MCP; MCP is the plumbing it uses, not what it teaches.

edges.evidence: add relevant context from your Microsoft 365 meetings and documents
edges.reason: Shows how to connect Work IQ so Copilot draws on meeting and document context, and traces a requirement to its implementation: grounding in team knowledge.

edges.evidence: with a human in the loop at each step
edges.reason: An app-modernization playbook; 'a human in the loop at each step' is one closing mention, not something the talk teaches.

edges.evidence: custom agents, agent skills, instructions files
edges.reason: Explains what each context building block (agent skills among them) is best at and how to standardize and distribute them across an organization.

edges.evidence: Fine-grained authorization for hosted MCP servers
edges.reason: The whole session is a pattern for per-identity authorization in front of hosted MCP servers.

edges.evidence: MCP servers, skills, and agents
edges.reason: Skills appear as one item in an internal catalog; the talk is about building the catalog and measuring adoption, so knowing skills helps but is not clearly assumed.

edges.evidence: opening a pull request
edges.reason: The demo has an agent open a pull request and route changes through a diff you approve; following it assumes you know what a pull request is.

edges.evidence: Coding agents can write and ship software quickly
edges.reason: Opens by taking coding agents that write and ship code as given and is about deciding what those agents should work on next.

edges.evidence: revoking and rotating the credential
edges.reason: A secrets-scanning procedure built around revoking and rotating credentials assumes you know what API keys and tokens are.

edges.evidence: every automated decision needs an audit trail
edges.reason: 'Every automated decision needs an audit trail' is one point in the healthcare segment; the talk does not teach how to build signed evidence or audit trails.

edges.evidence: each written by an AI agent
edges.reason: Case study of routing Jira tickets to Copilot cloud agents that opened hundreds of autonomous pull requests.

edges.evidence: how to connect Copilot activity to metrics your business cares about
edges.reason: Data on which signals separate deep AI adoption from shallow rollouts, and how to tie Copilot activity to business metrics.

edges.evidence: 460 pull requests a week
edges.reason: A Level 200 talk about an agent factory producing 460 pull requests a week assumes pull request basics; the quoted phrase is a statistic, but the assumption is sound.

edges.evidence: community into community-powered security impact
edges.reason: A blueprint for how one open source project built and scaled security practices across contributors and communities; the quoted phrase itself is vague.

edges.evidence: evidence-backed diagnosis and proposed fix
edges.reason: The agent uses observability data to diagnose a failure and propose a fix, and the talk covers where human review, escalation and a kill switch belong.

edges.evidence: fix issues before a pull request exists
edges.reason: Shows reviewing agent-written code for issues before a pull request exists and having Copilot help fix existing alerts.

edges.evidence: expose it through an MCP server
edges.reason: Hands-on workshop that exposes a knowledge base through an MCP server you build.

edges.evidence: code and pipelines it's meant to protect
edges.reason: Pipelines are named only as something backups must protect; following a backup-and-recovery talk does not need CI/CD knowledge.

edges.evidence: agent opens a pull request
edges.reason: Starts from an agent's pull request that passed CI and merged; assumes pull request basics.

edges.evidence: promote and demote autonomy safely, per decision class
edges.reason: About deciding how much autonomy an on-call agent gets, per decision class: what agents are allowed to do.
